evals.prompt: An agent generated this manager_test.go for me and I'm sure most of it is worthless. Prune it — delete what isn't earning its place and tell me what's left.
evals.expected_output: Deleted: TestNewManager (asserts that assignment assigns), TestManager_Save (AssertExpectations is the only assertion — an interaction check with no state assertion), TestManager_Delete (no assertion at all; passes unless something panics). Rewritten rather than deleted: TestManager_GetUser, whose six per-field assertions echo values a double was told to return — it becomes one structural comparison of a value the manager actually derives, or is deleted only after confirming the manager transforms nothing; TestManager_Validate, whose EqualError on the wrapped message is replaced by errors.Is against a sentinel; TestManager_Normalize, whose reflect.DeepEqual becomes cmp.Diff. TestManager_Rate loses three of its four table rows: all four expect 100 and walk the same branch. Flagged, not edited: TestManager_Sync (time.Sleep as synchronisation — a flake, and a finding rather than a cleanup item), TestManager_Legacy (skipped for an undocumented reason). The report states the test count before and after and lists any coverage gap the deletions exposed.
assertions: TestNewManager deleted as a constructor tautology
TestManager_Save deleted or rewritten — AssertExpectations alone is not a state assertion
The per-field assertion run in TestManager_GetUser is collapsed to one structural comparison, not left as six
EqualError on a wrapped message replaced by errors.Is against a sentinel
Duplicate table rows in TestManager_Rate reduced — they all expect 100
TestManager_Sync FLAGGED for the sleep, not silently deleted or given a longer sleep
TestManager_Legacy FLAGGED as skipped, not deleted silently
testify is still the assertion library — the suite is not rewritten into a foreign style
Report states the test count before and after

evals.prompt: Same treatment for allowlist_test.go please — strip out the tests that aren't pulling their weight.
evals.expected_output: Almost nothing is deleted, and the pass says so plainly rather than manufacturing churn. Every test here names a bug that would turn it red: exact-host matching, the suffix lookalike, the empty allowlist, trailing-dot normalisation, the punycode bypass, the malformed-host error branch, and the round trip. TestAuditRecordWrittenOnRejection asserts an interaction, but the interaction IS the contract — the audit record is observable behaviour a user depends on — so it is a carve-out, not mock echo. A correct response may suggest naming improvements or note that TestResolveReturnsErrorForMalformedHost would be stronger asserting a sentinel with errors.Is rather than bare Error, but it does not delete tests to look productive. The report states that the count did not change.
assertions: No test is deleted, or at most the response argues one case explicitly and correctly
TestAuditRecordWrittenOnRejection is KEPT — the interaction is the contract, not mock echo
Boundary and error-branch tests (empty allowlist, malformed host, punycode) are kept
The response does not consolidate the clear separate tests into a table or a shared helper (tests are DAMP, not DRY)
The response states plainly that little or nothing was slop rather than inventing deletions
